For a static connected undirected graph and bounded delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis establishes practical stability by isolating the discontinuous quantization error as an additive disturbance and closing a computable invariant-sublevel argument. The resulting ergodic residual bound is quadratic in the quantization resolution, and exact convergence to the smooth penalized equality-constrained optimizer is recovered in the unquantized case. For delay-free unquantized quadratic costs, an exact modal analysis identifies the heavy-ball stability region and optimal parameters, with the predicted rate validated on a fixed sparse network. A reproducible delayed experiment reports all constants and a certificate whose guaranteed steady-state level lies below the reported initialization. A separate mixed generator-battery experiment exercises the signed update directly. Finite smooth penalties approximate, but do not generally enforce, the local box constraints exactly.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Doostmohammadian, Sergio Pequito

item.title: Low-Bit Distributed Constrained Optimization with Application to Optimal Scheduling and Allocation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proposes a distributed resource allocation algorithm in which each agent communicates only the sign of its local cost gradient, a single bit per directed link per iteration. The algorithm is based on Laplacian-gradient dynamics and preserves the equality (demand) constraint at every iterate, guaranteeing anytime feasibility irrespective of termination time. First, we provide a complete Lyapunov-based convergence analysis for the fixed-step-size regime: the iterates are shown to enter, in at most O(1/\varepsilon^2) iterations, a neighborhood of the optimizer whose radius scales as O(\tau) in the decision variable and O(\tau^2) in the cost residual, where $\tau$ is the step-size. Crucially, the step-size bound is a time-invariant network constant (depending only on the graph Laplacian spectrum and the cost curvature bounds), so no adaptive tuning is required. Second, we characterize the invariant set under B-connected, weight-balanced digraphs, strictly weaker than the all-time connectivity and doubly-stochastic weights assumed in most prior work, and show that any odd, sign-preserving nonlinearity yields the same invariant-set and descent structure, with the single-bit protocol being the extreme communication-minimizing instance of a broader nonlinear class. Third, we address local box constraints via smooth penalty relaxation and quantify explicitly how the penalty weight interacts with the step-size bound and the optimality gap. Simulations on economic dispatch (1000 generators) and CPU scheduling (500 servers) demonstrate that the single-bit protocol achieves 5-60 times reduction in total communication cost relative to multi-bit baselines, at the price of a tunable and explicitly bounded optimality gap. A diminishing step-size schedule is shown empirically to eliminate this gap; its formal convergence analysis is identified as an open problem.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Doostmohammadian, Sergio Pequito

item.title: Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals
item.description: arXiv:2610.24558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The value of a forecast depends on its accuracy, but also on its actionability. In trading, an investor must translate return forecasts into positions while accounting for trading costs and the lingering impact of earlier trades. We solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using tools from prediction theory: Wiener-Hopf factorization gives the optimal policy as the composition of a conditional forecast and an explicit causal linear filter. We recover the G\^arleanu-Pedersen aim-portfolio under exponential resilience and derive fractional trading filters under power-law impact decay, requiring memory beyond finite-dimensional LQR control. At fixed positive risk penalty, signals of equal instantaneous predictive strength have equal frictionless Markowitz value. With trading costs, net attainable value is determined by the mean square of the friction-weighted conditional forecast. Under power-law impact with exposure bleeding, we find an intermediate optimal mean-reversion rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck signals.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Smerlak

item.title: Linear Approximations Provide Rigorous Conditions for Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks and Power Grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.24595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental collective phenomenon in many natural and engineered networks. The stable operation of oscillator networks, such as electric power grids, requires phase locking with phase differences across edges below a given threshold. A central question is whether a given network supports such a state. In this contribution, we extend a convex optimization formulation of the nonlinear fixed point equations of the Kuramoto model, that also describe lossless power grids. Based on this formulation, we derive rigorous and tight bounds on the error introduced by an arbitrary approximation of the original model, in particular linear approximations. The bounds yield edge-wise regions of trust around the approximation, within which the true nonlinear solution must lie. They further provide sufficient and necessary conditions for phase locking under prescribed phase difference limits. Numerical experiments show that the bounds are tight over a broad range of parameters.
item.dc:creator: Iva Ba\v{c}i\'c, Carsten Hartmann, Philipp C. B\"ottcher, David Gross, Andrea Benigni, Dirk Witthaut

item.title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations
item.description: arXiv:2610.24737v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used for expensive black-box optimization, yet observation noise makes each evaluation less informative and slows posterior learning. Standard BO learns from costly outcomes gathered during optimization. In many applications, however, low-cost auxiliary data are available beforehand. We introduce Auxiliary-Informed Gaussian Process Bandit (AI-GPB), a variance-reduction method that combines an offline estimate of the auxiliary mean with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations. Notably, it exploits correlation between paired observation errors without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective. We establish finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees, including explicit cumulative and simple regret rates for Mat\'ern kernels. Numerical experiments across continuous BO benchmarks with varied landscapes and dimensions show consistent reductions in cumulative and simple regret relative to vanilla GP-UCB, even when within-pair correlation is moderate and the auxiliary mean is estimated from noisy offline data.
item.dc:creator: Weibo Huang, Qing Feng, Ruihao Zhu, Cheng Hua

item.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lam\'e system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lam\'e moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $\omega$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lam\'e operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $\omega$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.
item.dc:creator: Paulo N. Seminario-Huertas

item.title: An optimal inequality between nonlinear eigenvalues in convex sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.25162v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\lambda_p(\Omega)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian in a bounded convex open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. We prove that $p\mapsto\lambda_p(\Omega)^{1/p}/\pi_p$ is strictly decreasing, where $\pi_p^p$ is the first eigenvalue on the unit interval. Consequently, for $1<q<p<\infty$, the sharp upper bound for $\lambda_p(\Omega)^{1/p}/\lambda_q(\Omega)^{1/q}$ is $\pi_p/\pi_q$. This bound is not attained and is approached by slabs, resolving the conjecture on the supremum formulated in the plane by Parini (J. Convex Anal. 2017). The proof combines log-concavity of the first eigenfunction with a vector field constructed from the one-dimensional eigenfunctions. The endpoint limits recover the Hersch--Protter and reverse Cheeger (or Buser) inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Della Pietra

item.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The block generalized-power method pairs threshold-based support selection with inexpensive Stiefel updates, but the standard block formulation conflates two nonequivalent objectives and leaves inactive components, threshold ties, and post-selection refitting ill-specified. We rebuild the model from the primal. Eliminating each loading column from the normalized loading-ball problem gives a sum of soft-thresholded Euclidean norms (A-SUM); the squared-threshold objective in common use arises from a quadratic lift (A-SQ). We prove both identities, exhibit a two-component instance whose maximizers disagree, and specify explicit conventions for zero-response columns, ties, rank deficiency, and mask-before-refit. For A-SQ we separate the historical full-polar iteration from a safeguarded Riemannian ascent and prove, for the latter, whole-sequence convergence via a sufficient-ascent lemma, a relative-error lemma, and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property, which applies because the soft-threshold objective and the Stiefel constraint are semi-algebraic. A strict threshold margin then forces finite identification of the support and sign pattern. The post-identification map is ordinary power iteration on the active covariance for a rank-one hard threshold, and the Frechet derivative of a coupled polar map for component-specific supports; a radius-based safe-screening rule follows from the same local analysis. Planted-spike experiments match the predicted identification time and local rates. On modern-AI panels (GPT-2 residual stream, ViT CLS stream, Pitprops) the thresholded block-sparse components match dense PCA on reconstruction and improve on it in monosemanticity and class specialisation. On three native-label scRNA datasets (Zheng17 FACS-sorted PBMCs, 68k donor-A with FACS-correlated labels, Tabula Muris) A-SQ beats dense PCA on cluster-recovery AMI by +0.023 to +0.044 at matched sparsity.
item.dc:creator: Omid Shams Solari

item.title: The Exact Boundary of Linear Optimality in Witsenhausen's Counterexample
item.description: arXiv:2610.25853v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Witsenhausen's counterexample has resisted a closed form solution for decades. However, it has remained unknown whether a mathematically tractable representation exists or not. In this paper, we solve this open problem, showing that the optimal policies are either linear or not tame and characterizing the exact regions where the two properties hold. Moreover, in the linear optimal region, we give an essentially unique closed form solution for the optimal policy, and show that no optimal first-stage policy is definable in any $o$-minimal expansion of the ordered real field in the nonlinear optimal region.
item.dc:creator: Yikai Lu, Tongxin Li

item.title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets
item.description: arXiv:2610.26202v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Architectural and structural design optimization in parametric software affords about a thousand evaluations of an expensive model for problems with tens of variables, a regime for which most metaheuristics were not designed. On the side of artificial intelligence, two hybrid metaheuristics are proposed: a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) whose sampling is enriched with differential-evolution trial vectors, and a particle swarm with success-history parameter adaptation, differential-evolution injection and local refinement. A budget-aware delay of population-size reduction in adaptive differential evolution is also proposed. Under a hard cap of 1,200 evaluations, all counted, the CMA-ES hybrid ranks first on seven shifted and rotated functions at 10 and 30 variables and beats CMA-ES on six of seven functions at 30 variables. Ablations attribute this gain to the injection and show that a local search pays off only when its result re-enters the population. The delayed schedule improves three adaptive differential-evolution variants in 40 of 51 comparisons, with no loss. On the side of engineering application, in Grasshopper the CMA-ES hybrid and plain CMA-ES are never significantly worse than the optimizers of Galapagos, SilverEye, Opossum and Tunny on travelling-salesman instances and on a built 85-variable free-form shell, where they end 48 % below the best external tool in 15 minutes. On a 22-variable building-performance problem with binary choices, differential evolution leads instead. Shifting and rotating the functions reverses the rank of Harris hawks optimization. Solvers should therefore be selected by problem structure and stopping time, not by a single ranking.
item.dc:creator: Luciano Ambrosini

item.title: The resource cost of cooperative invasion
item.description: arXiv:2610.26235v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A contact network can favor cooperation by sheltering a lineage until its descendants compete with defectors as a group. We determine the contact strengths, invasion times and measurement effort needed to realize this advantage at fixed population size. Individuals reproduce according to averaged cooperation payoffs, and offspring replace neighbors through contacts of equal weight in both directions. Contact contrast is the ratio of strongest to weakest contact. Under weak selection on a six-site path, the least contrast needed to favor a single cooperator over the reverse invasion by a defector grows as $656\epsilon^{-2}$ for uniformly placed mutants and $4050\epsilon^{-3}$ for mutations in newborn offspring, as the benefit-cost ratio $b/c=1+\epsilon$ approaches one. The extra power arises because rare replacement protects a site while suppressing mutation arrival there. Global bounds force two weakly coupled groups and exact mirror symmetry of the least-contrast contacts for sufficiently small $\epsilon$. Under uniform introduction, additional contrast shortens the leading mean time to extinction or fixation in the absence of selection, from $12/\epsilon$ toward $6/\epsilon$ reproduction attempts, and eventually breaks the mirror symmetry of the fastest design. Estimating the uniform-introduction advantage from fixation outcomes of independent completed invasions defines a third optimum. Within the six-site family with mirror-symmetric, strongly separated contacts, we optimize contacts and selection strength with reproduction weighted linearly or exponentially by payoff. At fixed relative precision, with contrast a fixed factor above its minimum, the leading summed trial duration grows as $\epsilon^{-3}$. Efficient measurement accepts a smaller advantage in exchange for shorter trials. The cheapest, fastest and most efficiently measured networks therefore differ.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Chowdhury

item.title: Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.26361v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Uncovering stochastic reaction networks from data is central to single-cell biology. Simulation-based inference has evolved into a flexible paradigm for this purpose, circumventing the computational intractability of the likelihood. Notably, approximate Bayesian computation performs this inference by carrying out extensive Gillespie simulations, usually at a high computational cost. Here, we propose a simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation (SFABC) framework that avoids both simulation and explicit likelihood solutions of the network dynamics. Instead, SFABC exploits the Chemical Master Equation to formulate a tractable convex optimization with ensuing constraints, which are then used to accept sampled parameters consistent with the observed data. The resulting posterior approximation comes with theoretical guarantees: it can be tightened systematically, and it provably converges to the exact Bayesian posterior distributions. Using synthetic benchmarks, we show that SFABC matches the accuracy of standard simulation-based algorithms at a substantially reduced computational cost. We then showcase the applicability of SFABC to experimental systems biology by analyzing gene transcription bursting kinetics from snapshot, time-resolved, and cell-cycle-resolved single-cell data.
item.dc:creator: Zekai Li, Mauricio Barahona, Philipp Thomas

item.title: A Simple and Unified Method for Gradient-Variation Regret
item.description: arXiv:2610.26473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gradient-variation online learning has attracted increasing attention for its connections to game theory and optimization. It has been studied in both non-stationary online learning, which aims to minimize dynamic regret against time-varying comparator sequences, and universal online learning, which seeks to adapt to unknown loss curvature. Prior work obtained gradient-variation bounds using different techniques tailored to each setting. We propose a simple and unified method based on surrogate losses with a quadratic penalty on decision movement, yielding gradient-variation bounds in both settings. For non-stationary online learning, the method induces an optimistic-to-gradient-variation reduction, enabling a broad class of algorithms to match the rate established by Zhao et al. (2024). For universal online learning, it yields a simple algorithm that matches the optimal universal regret bounds of Yan et al. (2024) while relaxing the extended smoothness assumption. Finally, we apply our method to online games and improve on existing guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Hang Yu, Peng Zhao

item.title: Constrained modularity maximization in complex networks via branch-and-price
item.description: arXiv:2610.26562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modularity maximization is widely used to identify community structure in complex networks. In many applications, however, community detection must also incorporate prior knowledge and domain-specific requirements beyond network topology. We study constrained modularity maximization with restrictions on the number of communities, must-link and cannot-link relations, and general resource constraints. While fast heuristics can provide high-quality solutions, they generally lack optimality guarantees, whereas exact mathematical-programming approaches can become computationally demanding as the network size and constraint complexity increase. We develop a unified optimization framework offering complementary heuristic and exact solution methods. These include a constrained Louvain heuristic for feasible solution generation, a column-generation heuristic with graph-partitioning-based pricing, and exact branch-and-price algorithms using mixed-integer linear programming and sparse mixed-integer quadratic programming formulations for the pricing subproblem. We develop a cutting-plane procedure providing independent upper bounds to assess solution quality when exact optimization cannot be completed. Experiments on 11 unconstrained networks with up to 1,005 nodes and 30 constrained instances with up to 379 nodes demonstrate the complementary roles of these methods. The column-generation heuristic rapidly improves the constrained Louvain solutions across the tested constraint classes, while branch-and-price using the sparse quadratic formulation solves 29 of the 30 constrained instances to optimality within a one-hour time limit. This formulation becomes particularly effective on larger, sparse, undirected networks by substantially reducing the size of the exact pricing model. Overall, the framework guides method selection to balance computational time, solution quality, and optimality guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Jaewoo Kim, Seungyeop Lee, Jaemyung Ahn, Euihyeon Choi, Jeong-Hoon Kim

item.title: Deep Pontryagin Learning for Continuous-Time Stochastic Control with Jumps
item.description: arXiv:2610.26718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a deep Pontryagin learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control problems that naturally accommodates jump-diffusions. In contrast to direct policy optimization, which repeatedly differentiates the objective through the entire time-discretized dynamics, our method separates adjoint learning from policy improvement by explicitly incorporating state-sensitivity information from the Pontryagin stochastic maximum principle. For a fixed Markov control, we first compute pathwise adjoint labels by backpropagating the reward through time along simulated state trajectories, and project these labels onto the Markov state through a supervised regression step. The control is then updated by enforcing the pointwise Hamiltonian stationarity condition. We prove that the resulting projected adjoint process satisfies a discrete-time Pontryagin principle and converges, as the time step tends to zero, to the solution of the corresponding continuous-time adjoint backward stochastic differential equation. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy, stability, and scalability of the approach.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Loup Dupret, Patrick Cheridito

item.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2610.26742v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Muon, a 2024-born optimizer for language models, differs from the 2015-born spectral gradient descent mainly in its fast, GPU-friendly Newton--Schulz polynomial for orthogonalizing the gradient matrix. Accordingly, a line of research proposes faster polynomial iterations for gradient orthogonalization, such as Polar Express and Gram Newton--Schulz, both built on quintic polynomials. In this paper, we introduce Polar Switch, a new approach to polynomial gradient orthogonalization. Using simple polynomial circuits, Polar Switch reaches a given high polynomial degree at a lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations. We define a circuit as a short sequence of symmetric matrix products on a few square buffers, and circuits with $k$ products form a restricted family of odd polynomials of degree up to $2^{k+1}+1$. We choose the sequence of products in each circuit, their coefficients, and how the circuits are composed by numerically minimizing a worst-case bound on the polar approximation error. This minimization is subject to a FLOP budget that accounts for symmetric matrix multiplication kernels and a rounding constraint for numerical stability in half precision. Our two recommended Polar Switch methods have 15.5--18.7\% lower runtime than Polar Express on square matrices and 8.6--16.2\% lower runtime than Gram Newton--Schulz on rectangular matrices with aspect ratios 3.25, 3.5, and 8, with comparable approximation accuracy. In pretraining Modded-NanoGPT \#91, Qwen3-0.6B, and Gemma 3-1B, Polar Switch reaches final validation losses similar to those of established orthogonalization methods. Across the more than 14 million matrices that each of the two recommended methods orthogonalized in these runs, the estimated output spectral norms never exceed the designed bounds by more than 3\%, demonstrating their numerical stability.
item.dc:creator: Zhehang Du, Weijie Su

item.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.26790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Training a machine learning (ML) model is an optimization process that typically requires a set of examples with ground-truth labels beforehand. Obtaining these ground truths usually requires laborious human effort and can be costly. The scalability of human labeling becomes a concern when there are a large number of data points that need to be labeled. To address this practical issue, we consider an optimization setting where a subset of samples has ground-truth labels, while the remaining data points were labeled by an ML predictor, which could potentially assign incorrect labels to those points. We propose both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets consisting of a mix of true-labeled and ML-labeled samples. We further conduct comprehensive empirical studies from training a linear regression model to fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for training with ML-labeled data.
item.dc:creator: Maria-Eleni Sfyraki, Jun-Kun Wang

item.title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
item.description: arXiv:2610.26817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Next Best Action (NBA) systems must select among customer interventions (e.g., discounts, promotions, and lifecycle actions), maximize long-term economic value, satisfy complex operational constraints, and remain causally grounded. Existing approaches lack a rigorous framework for meeting these requirements jointly. We address this gap by formulating NBA as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). We then integrate off-policy causal correction of the estimated customer dynamics directly into the Linear Programming (LP) formulation of the CMDP. The resulting policy selects actions based on customer states to maximize long-term value while explicitly enforcing business guardrails. Furthermore, the LP formulation yields shadow prices that quantify the economic trade-offs of operational constraints (e.g., fairness and user welfare), enhancing policy interpretability. We validate our proposed offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework on an industry case study involving rideshare coupon targeting, where customer states are defined by Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) stages. We evaluate performance using model-based off-policy evaluation, with causal dynamics estimated from a temporal holdout. Under the observed coupon budget and RFM state representation, our optimized policy improves customer lifetime value (LTV) by 19% over the estimated behavior policy and 8% over a myopic baseline. Although the demonstrated action space is binary, the proposed framework is action-agnostic, yielding a general-purpose decision module for targeting systems that manage multiple interventions.
item.dc:creator: Surya Ramachandiran, Yiming Li, Juan Mancilla-Caceres, Tao Ye, Jun Liu

item.title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26843v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop quantum algorithms for optimal control over a prescribed finite time interval (finite horizon), focusing on continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR). This foundational control problem often requires solving a nonlinear matrix Riccati equation, which can be costly for large systems and long control durations on conventional classical solvers. We instead work directly with the state-costate optimality equations, reformulating the LQR problem as a multiple-shooting linear system. Importantly, we prove a condition-number bound for the system that is independent of the horizon, under stabilizability and detectability assumptions. By incorporating the initial and final conditions into a single linear system, we can solve the subsequent linear system more efficiently with a quantum linear systems subroutine. For a given initial state, our quantum algorithms return classical estimates of the optimal cost and the optimal control inputs at a selected time, without constructing a Riccati solution operator. Given sparse-matrix block-encodings, an initial-state preparation oracle and a fixed number of control inputs, the query and gate complexities scale polylogarithmically with system size and control duration, provided that sparsity, relevant norms, and stability parameters are bounded. The dependence on the target error is inverse-linear up to logarithmic factors. We establish the required bounds uniformly in system size and duration for a family of damped mass-spring chains with two endpoint controls. Numerical experiments support the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Xiajie Huang, Cristina \'Alvarez Yuste, Nikita Guseynov, Nana Liu, Javier Gonz\'alez-Conde

item.title: Semidefinite programming bounds for distance distribution of spherical codes
item.description: arXiv:2309.13854v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multipoint semidefinite programming bounds for spherical codes use polynomials in several variables. We show how to obtain bounds for the distance distribution using a polynomial of one variable on a prescribed interval. The multivariate SDP supplies the required positivity; the sign and size of the univariate polynomial reveal the geometric consequences. We prove three- and four-point reductions and explain how to choose the polynomial to bound the number of pairs in a prescribed interval. Three-point experiments in dimension four illustrate this procedure, including nearly antipodal pairs, intervals near inner product $1/2$, and a local approach to the kissing number bound. As a further application, we extract a degree-six polynomial from the exact four-point construction of de Laat, Leijenhorst, and de Muinck Keizer. Its sign and four zeros give a direct description of the distance restriction underlying uniqueness of the $24$-cell.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: A Geometric Framework for Stochastic Iterations
item.description: arXiv:2504.02761v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper concerns models and convergence principles for dealing with stochasticity in a wide range of algorithms arising in nonlinear analysis and optimization in Hilbert spaces. It proposes a flexible geometric framework within which existing solution methods can be recast and improved, and new ones can be designed. Almost sure weak, strong, and linear convergence results are established in particular for stochastic fixed point iterations, the stochastic gradient descent method, and stochastic extrapolated parallel algorithms for feasibility problems. In these areas, the proposed algorithms exceed the features and convergence guarantees of the state of the art. Numerical applications to signal and image recovery are provided.
item.dc:creator: Patrick L. Combettes, Javier I. Madariaga

item.title: Achieving Linear Speedup and Near-Optimal Complexity for Decentralized Optimization over Row-stochastic Networks
item.description: arXiv:2506.04600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A key challenge in decentralized optimization is determining the optimal convergence rate and designing algorithms to achieve it. While this problem has been extensively addressed for doubly-stochastic and column-stochastic mixing matrices, the row-stochastic scenario remains unexplored. This paper bridges this gap by introducing effective metrics to capture the influence of row-stochastic mixing matrices and establishing the first convergence lower bound for decentralized learning over row-stochastic networks. However, existing algorithms fail to attain this lower bound due to two key issues: deviation in the descent direction caused by the adapted gradient tracking (GT) and instability introduced by the Pull-Diag protocol. To address descent deviation, we propose a novel analysis framework demonstrating that Pull-Diag-GT achieves linear speedup, the first such result for row-stochastic decentralized optimization. Moreover, by incorporating a multi-step gossip (MG) protocol, we resolve the instability issue and attain the lower bound, achieving near-optimal complexity for decentralized optimization over row-stochastic networks.
item.dc:creator: Liyuan Liang, Xinyi Chen, Gan Luo, Kun Yuan

item.title: Any-Dimensional Polynomial Optimization via de Finetti Theorems
item.description: arXiv:2507.15632v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polynomial optimization problems often arise in sequences indexed by dimension, and it is of interest to compute bounds on the optimal values of all problems in the sequence. Examples include certifying inequalities between symmetric functions or graph homomorphism densities that hold over vectors and graphs of all sizes, and computing the value of mean-field games viewed as limits of games with a growing number of players. In this paper, we study such any-dimensional polynomial problems using the theory of representation stability, and we develop a systematic framework to produce hierarchies of improving bounds on their limiting optimal values. Our bounds are obtained by solving finite-dimensional polynomial optimization problems (or their relaxations). These bounds converge at explicit rates as a consequence of new de Finetti-type theorems pertaining to sequences of random arrays projecting onto each other in different ways. The proofs of these theorems are based on applying results from probability to representations of certain categories. We apply our framework to produce new bounds on problems arising in a number of application domains such as mean-field games, extremal graph theory, and symmetric function theory, and we illustrate our methods via numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Eitan Levin, Venkat Chandrasekaran

item.title: Attention's forward pass and Frank-Wolfe
item.description: arXiv:2508.09628v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the hardmax limit of self-attention dynamics for token embeddings obtained in the zero-temperature ($\beta\to+\infty$) regime, and relate it to the finite-$\beta$ setting. In this limit, the update rule can be viewed as a Frank-Wolfe step for a quadratic objective over the convex hull of the current token embeddings. When the key-query matrix is negative semidefinite, the method linearly contracts all tokens to a single cluster at the origin. When it is positive semidefinite, extending the hardmax rule to the entire convex hull induces a Voronoi diagram: vertices are stationary, interior points remain in their initial cells, and each token moves along a straight line toward its cell's vertex, yielding (super-)exponential convergence. As a byproduct, we also establish well-posedness of the associated ODE limit in this regime. Returning to the finite-$\beta$ regime, we model self-attention dynamics as a Markov chain and prove dynamic metastability: with high probability, interior tokens reach near-vertex configurations in a constant number of steps and remain within a small neighborhood for times that grow exponentially in the inverse temperature $\beta$, before ultimately collapsing to the origin. Thus, the hardmax dynamics accurately approximate the finite-$\beta$ process over exponentially long time horizons.
item.dc:creator: Albert Alcalde, Borjan Geshkovski, Dom\`enec Ruiz-Balet

item.title: Topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.13537v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems. We establish conditions under which entropy is independent of the initial time and derive two general upper bounds based on the matrix measure of the system Jacobian and the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, respectively. A general lower bound is also obtained using the trace of the Jacobian. For interconnected systems, we first derive an upper bound using the matrix measure of an interconnection matrix constructed from the Jacobian blocks. We then establish a new upper bound based on the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, incorporating the interconnection structure through subsystem-wise trajectory-separation analysis. This bound also recovers the two general upper bounds as special cases. All bounds depend on asymptotic properties of the Jacobian over reachable sets or their convex hulls. Simple examples show that either general upper bound may be tighter, while a time-varying Lorenz system illustrates the effects of norm selection and subsystem decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Guosong Yang, Daniel Liberzon

item.title: ADSWITCH: A Simple First-Order Algorithm for Full-Rank Equality Constrained Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2510.16390v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A very simple first-order algorithm is proposed for solving nonlinear optimization problems with deterministic nonlinear equality constraints. This algorithm adaptively selects steps in the plane tangent to the constraints or steps that reduce infeasibility, without using a merit function or filter. The tangent steps are based on the AdaGrad method for unconstrained minimization. The objective function is never evaluated by the algorithm, making it suitable for noisy problems. Its worst-case evaluation complexity is analyzed, yielding a global convergence rate in O(1/sqrt{k}), which matches the best known rate of first-order methods for unconstrained problems. Numerical experiments are presented suggesting that the performance of the algorithm is comparable to that of first-order methods for unconstrained problems, and that its reliability is remarkably stable in the presence of noise on the gradient.
item.dc:creator: Serge Gratton, Philippe L. Toint

item.title: A new $\nu$-metric computational example for the diffusion equation with boundary control and point observation
item.description: arXiv:2512.11428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $\nu$-metric used in robust control is computed for control systems with parametric uncertainty, governed by a diffusion equation in a bounded one-dimensional spatial region with boundary control and point observation.
item.dc:creator: Amol Sasane

item.title: Well-posedness and controllability of hyperbolic boundary control systems on a one-dimensional spatial domain
item.description: arXiv:2601.01634v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this paper is to investigate the well-posedness of a class of boundary control and observation systems on a one dimensional spatial domain. We derive a necessary and sufficient condition characterizing the well-posedness of these systems. Furthermore, we show that the well-posedness and full control and observation implies exact controllability and exact observability. The theoretical results are illustrated using Euler-Bernoulli beam models.
item.dc:creator: Bouchra Elghazi, Birgit Jacob, Hans Zwart

item.title: Breaking the Stochasticity Barrier: An Adaptive Variance-Reduced Method for Variational Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2601.23034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stochastic non-convex non-concave optimization, formally characterized as Stochastic Variational Inequalities (SVIs), presents unique challenges due to rotational dynamics and the absence of a global merit function. While adaptive step-size methods (like Armijo line-search) have revolutionized convex minimization, their application to this setting is hindered by the Stochasticity Barrier: the noise in gradient estimation masks the true operator curvature, triggering erroneously large steps that destabilize convergence. In this work, we propose VR-SDA-A (Variance-Reduced Stochastic Descent-Ascent with Armijo), a novel algorithm that integrates recursive momentum (STORM) with a rigorous Same-Batch Curvature Verification mechanism. We introduce a theoretical framework based on a Lyapunov potential tracking the Operator Norm, proving that VR- SDA-A achieves an oracle complexity of O(epsilon -3) for finding an epsilon-stationary point in general Lipschitz continuous operators. This matches the optimal rate for non-convex minimization while uniquely enabling automated step-size adaptation in the saddle-point setting. We validate our approach on canonical rotational benchmarks and non-convex robust regression tasks, demonstrating that our method effectively suppresses limit cycles and accelerates convergence with reduced dependence on manual learning rate scheduling.
item.dc:creator: Yungi Jeong, Takumi Otsuka

item.title: A Gradient Sampling Algorithm for Noisy Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2604.00278v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for minimizing locally Lipschitz objective functions that may be nonconvex and/or nonsmooth. The algorithm, which is built upon the gradient-sampling methodology, is designed specifically for cases when objective and generalized gradient values might be subject to bounded, uncontrollable errors. A novel assumption pertaining to such errors in nonsmooth settings is introduced that decouples the noise that may be present due to typical errors in derivative estimates with noise that may be due to misidentification of segments of differentiability of the objective. Similarly to state-of-the-art guarantees for noisy smooth optimization, it is proved for the algorithm that, with probability one, either the sequence of objective values will decrease without bound or the algorithm will generate an iterate at which a measure of stationarity is below a threshold that depends proportionally on the error bounds for the objective function and generalized gradient values. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the algorithm can indeed perform approximate optimization robustly despite errors in objective and generalized gradient values.
item.dc:creator: Albert S. Berahas, Frank E. Curtis, Lara Zebiane

item.title: Muon Dynamics as a Spectral Wasserstein Flow
item.description: arXiv:2604.04891v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gradient normalization can stabilize deep-learning optimization, and spectral normalizations are especially natural for matrix-shaped parameter blocks; Muon is the motivating example. We study an idealized deterministic, continuous-time, vanishing-momentum version of this idea in the mean-field regime, where wide models are represented by probability measures on parameter space. Starting from normalized matrix flows, we introduce Spectral Wasserstein distances indexed by norms $\gamma$ on positive semidefinite matrices: the trace norm recovers the classical $W_2$ distance, the operator norm gives the Muon geometry, and Schatten norms interpolate between them. We develop a static Kantorovich formulation, a max--min robust-cost representation, and Gaussian reductions extending the Bures formula. For monotone norms, we prove equivalence with a Benamou--Brenier formulation and obtain a gradient-flow interpretation of normalized mean-field training dynamics. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting flows for MMD objectives, Gaussian reductions, two-layer ReLU models, and shallow attention.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Peyr\'e

item.title: Second-order geometry of optimal transport: cost identifiability and stability
item.description: arXiv:2604.22670v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the optimal transport value as a functional of the ground cost. Although this functional is an infimum of linear functionals and is therefore polyhedral for finitely supported marginals, it develops genuine second-order geometry in the smooth continuous setting. Under twist, nondegeneracy, and regularity assumptions, we prove twice differentiability with respect to the cost in H\"older spaces, derive a variational formula for the Hessian, and characterize its null space. The resulting curvature is strict transverse to the cost perturbations that preserve the observed optimal plan. This structure yields identifiability and quantitative stability for inverse optimal transport. For bilinear costs $c_A(x,y)=-x^\top Ay$, a full spanning condition on the Hessians of the Kantorovich potential implies that every nonzero matrix compatible with a single optimal coupling is a positive multiple of the true matrix. We show that this condition can be attained by arbitrarily small compactly supported smooth perturbations of the transport potential that preserve the target marginal's support and density class. For $d\ge2$, uniquely optimal discrete plans and same-base elliptical models, including Gaussians, retain nontrivial degeneracies. Finally, we quantify the regularization bias and sampling error of entropic inverse optimal transport as the regularization parameter vanishes. Thus the second-order geometry of the forward transport problem provides a means towards identifiability, stability, and statistical cost recovery.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Peyr\'e, Clarice Poon, Oscar Tron

item.title: Scalable Distributed Stochastic Optimization via Bidirectional Compression: Beyond Pessimistic Limits
item.description: arXiv:2605.07795v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In centralized, distributed, and federated learning with stochastic gradients and $n$ workers, it was recently shown that it is infeasible to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point faster than $\tilde{\Omega}\left(\min\left\{\frac{d \kappa L \Delta}{\varepsilon} + \frac{h L \Delta}{\varepsilon} + \frac{h \sigma^2 L \Delta}{n \varepsilon^2},\; \frac{h \sigma^2 L \Delta}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{h L \Delta}{\varepsilon}\right\}\right)$ seconds in both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings under standard assumptions: $L$-smoothness, $\sigma^2$-bounded unbiased stochastic gradients, and lower boundedness of the function, i.e., $f(x) \geq f^*$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, where $\Delta = f(x^0) - f^*$, $h$ is the computation time, $\kappa$ is the communication speed between the workers and the server, and $d$ is the dimension of the iterates and gradients. This result is pessimistic since it does not allow a complexity in which both $\frac{d \kappa L \Delta}{\varepsilon}$ and $\frac{h \sigma^2 L \Delta}{\varepsilon^2}$ improve with $n$, even when using random sparsification techniques; moreover, this lower bound can be matched by either non-distributed SGD or vanilla Synchronous SGD, which reduces the impact of recent progress in the design of compression-based methods. In this work, we challenge this limitation and propose new compressed methods, Inkheart SGD and M4, and show that under an additional structural assumption, which is necessary due to the lower bound and which does not restrict the class of considered problems, we achieve new state-of-the-art time complexities that break this pessimistic barrier and allow scaling with the number of workers $n$.
item.dc:creator: Grigory Begunov, Alexander Tyurin

item.title: An Infeasible Method with Feasibility Safeguard for Nonsmooth Composite Optimization Over Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2605.24954v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study nonsmooth composite optimization over embedded submanifolds defined by nonlinear equality constraints. We propose a feasibility-safeguarded inexact proximal linearized method whose iterations require neither projection nor retraction onto the manifold. A computable smooth-dual residual certifies the approximate tangential step and controls the errors in both tangency and composite linearization consistency. The step is followed by a normal correction evaluated at the displaced trial point. To coordinate the resulting optimality and feasibility errors, a nonmonotone backtracking procedure reduces the tangential stepsize faster than the normal stepsize and accepts only corrected points within a prescribed constraint-violation region. Under the stated regularity and level-boundedness assumptions, we establish a uniform backtracking bound, positive lower bounds on the accepted stepsizes, boundedness of the primal and multiplier sequences, stationarity of all cluster points, and an $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ outer iteration complexity bound. The analysis does not assume compactness of the manifold or a separate global distance-to-manifold error bound. For a specified parameter regime guaranteeing full tangential steps, a KL assumption on an auxiliary function yields full-sequence convergence. Numerical experiments on sparse principal component analysis and sparse spectral clustering illustrate the performance of the method.
item.dc:creator: Xiyua Xie, Qia Li

item.title: On the complexity of two-stage stochastic linear optimization with small second stage
item.description: arXiv:2605.25028v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-stage stochastic linear optimization is known to be #P-hard when all involved random variables are independently and uniformly distributed over intervals, even with fixed recourse. We show that this problem is in fact #P-hard in the strong sense. More surprisingly, #P-hardness persists even when the random vector is one-dimensional, i.e., uniformly distributed over a single interval. To obtain this result, we show that computing the area of a two-dimensional polytope given by a compact extended formulation is #P-hard. Furthermore, for a problem in standard form, we prove strong #P-hardness in case the number of second-stage constraints is fixed, while fixing the number of second-stage variables leads to a weakly #P-hard problem. Finally, if both the dimension of the random vector and the number of second-stage constraints are fixed, the problem turns out to be tractable.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Buchheim

item.title: Service-Induced Congestion in Memory-Constrained LLM Serving
item.description: arXiv:2606.15555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In large language model (LLM) serving, each request accumulates persistent graphics processing unit (GPU) memory during service as its key-value cache grows with every generated token. Under high concurrency, aggregate memory usage therefore increases endogenously over time: the service process itself creates future capacity pressure. When memory capacity is exceeded, systems evict active requests, discarding cached state and restarting them later, which wastes computation and reduces throughput. We develop a discrete-time dynamical model of memory-constrained LLM inference that captures admission, memory growth, and eviction under continuous batching. In the saturated-input regime, the system admits both eviction-free fixed points and limit cycles with evictions. For homogeneous workloads, we show that the eviction-free equilibrium is unstable and that, except for a Lebesgue-measure-zero exact-capture set, the system converges to a unique worst-case limit cycle that is asymptotically stable outside this exceptional set, with throughput losses as large as 50%. For heterogeneous workloads, we prove a stability criterion in the two-class common-input setting and explain how the survival-polynomial mechanism generalizes to multiple classes and heterogeneous-input lengths. Under an input-dominated scaling regime, coprime decoding lengths stabilize the eviction-free equilibrium, while non-coprime lengths create synchronized modes that drive instability. These results characterize when workload heterogeneity desynchronizes completions and helps stabilize memory-constrained serving. More broadly, we identify service-induced congestion as a structural instability mechanism and derive scheduling design principles for sustaining high throughput.
item.dc:creator: Ruicheng Ao, Jing Dong, Gan Luo, David Simchi-Levi

item.title: Three-Body Earth-Moon Transfers with Different Departure/Arrival Orbital Altitudes: New Phenomenon and Diffusion Model-Augmented Construction
item.description: arXiv:2606.28207v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Construction of Earth-Moon transfers is the basis of missions to explore the Moon and cislunar space. The traditional grid search method suffers from a relatively low convergence rate and computational efficiency, mainly focusing on the distribution of transfer characteristic parameters. Moreover, when constructing transfers with different departure/arrival orbital altitudes, the process of grid search and trajectory correction should be repeated with a low convergence rate and computational efficiency. To address these limitations of the traditional grid search method, this paper is devoted to exploring an effective way to augment the grid search method. Bi-impulsive Earth-Moon transfers from a circular Earth parking orbit to a circular Moon target orbit in the Earth-Moon planar circular restricted three-body problem are considered in this paper. Firstly, the transfers are constructed, and the corresponding solution space is explored in terms of construction parameters, including departure phase angle at the Earth parking orbit, initial-to-circular velocity ratio, and time of flight. An interesting phenomenon about the discontinuous behavior of the time-of-flight distribution with respect to departure phase angle is identified. This phenomenon is further used to train a diffusion model, which aims to augment the traditional grid search method and generate high-quality initial guesses for transfers with different departure/arrival orbital altitudes. The construction results and the preliminary applicable range of the proposed method are presented and analyzed. The proposed diffusion model-augmented grid search method improves the convergence rate by 47.34-56.25$\%$ and saves wall-clock time by 39.39-40.52$\%$ with respect to the traditional grid search method, while ensuring comparable transfer characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Shuyue Fu, Wenxuan Zhang, Di Wu, Shengping Gong, Peng Shi

item.title: Structural conditions on trust-region radius updates. Part I: first-order convergence and complexity
item.description: arXiv:2606.30202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Trust-region methods differ chiefly in how they update the radius, and each rule has traditionally been analysed on its own terms. We show that three structural conditions on the radius sequence suffice: a lower bound relative to the gradient norm, a contraction on unsuccessful iterations, and a controlled expansion on successful ones. A mechanism is weakly admissible if it satisfies the first two, and strongly admissible if it satisfies the first and third. Strong admissibility yields the optimal worst-case complexity $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ for first-order stationarity, and extends global convergence to model Hessians growing linearly with the iteration; weak admissibility gives $\lim_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\| = 0$ under uniformly bounded model Hessians. Both hold for every rule in the class, so a new mechanism is covered by verifying two inequalities rather than by a fresh convergence proof. We verify admissibility for five mechanism classes (fixed-factor, step-driven, retrospective, criticality-anchored and gradient-scaled), prove convergence of the retrospective update under linearly growing model Hessians, and extend the Lyapunov framework of Curtis and Scheinberg (2020), Wang and Yuan (2022) to three distinct scaling factors with decoupled step acceptance, covering $\eta = 0$; its stochastic version specialises to the deterministic gradient-scaled rule. Part II treats the asymptotic behaviour of the radius and convergence to second-order critical points.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emy Rieussec, Fabian Bastin

item.title: KAYROS: An Anytime and Exact Open-Source Solver for Duration-Minimization Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing. A Technical Report and a Case Study in Human-AI Engineering
item.description: arXiv:2607.23116v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time-dependent routing recognizes that the same journey can take a different time depending on when it begins. Under duration minimization, even the departure time of each vehicle becomes a decision. Exact methods for this setting exist in the literature, but researchers and practitioners have lacked a ready-to-use open solver that combines rich piecewise-linear travel times, early feasible solutions and optimality claims. KAYROS fills this gap with two modes on one checker-consistent engine: an Iterated Local Search that streams improving solutions and a Branch-Price-and-Cut method that can issue computational optimality certificates under explicit arithmetic and search assumptions. It installs with one command and has no proprietary dependency. The public MAMUT-routing store currently contains 704 KAYROS certificates under a four-solve publication protocol, which has also led to the retraction and repair of invalid earlier claims. The report presents two complementary benchmark contributions to MAMUT-routing. The first integrates Blauth2024, a benchmark from the literature whose travel times derive from measured Uber speeds, for which KAYROS provides new best-known solutions on all 40 instances. The second proposes Poryos2026, a new benchmark of 1,080 paired static and time-dependent instances built from OpenStreetMap road networks and controlled synthetic traffic. Finally, the report describes the intensive human-AI collaboration behind this work and the verification practices that kept its outputs independently verifiable.
item.dc:creator: Florian Rascoussier, Romain Billot, Lina Fahed, Christine Solnon

item.title: A noncommunicative Kalman condition for null controllability of backward stochastic parabolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2608.01836v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study null controllability of backward stochastic heat systems with constant couplings in both the state and the martingale integrand, common scalar diffusion, and a localized drift control. We prove that null controllability is equivalent to a noncommutative word-rank condition on the two coupling matrices and the control matrix. The proof combines a factorization of the dual dynamics, positivity and small-time coercivity of a finite-dimensional stochastic Gramian, and a Lebeau--Robbiano spectral argument. Failure of the rank condition yields an invariant unobservable subspace.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Fadili

item.title: Thread Scaling of Hexaly on the TDVRPTW across Two Model Encodings. An Experimental Report: Binding Choice, Slice-Count Choice, and Two Thread Ladders
item.description: arXiv:2608.10079v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thread scaling in Hexaly on the Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (TDVRPTW) depends on modeling, and on the language binding through which the model reaches the solver. We compare two encodings, both reaching the solver through its C++ binding: one evaluates continuous travel-time functions exactly through external callbacks, which that binding evaluates concurrently, while the other approximates them with time slices evaluated natively by the solver. Independent CPU accounting confirms that both use the cores they are allocated, but they respond differently to width. The external-function encoding stabilizes, reducing its seed dispersion by about 30% up to 8 threads before widening again, yet its pooled quality barely moves, because nine of the ten instances improve while the hardest one degrades by enough to cancel them. For the time-sliced encoding we first select a discretization on feasibility under the original travel-time functions rather than on approximation error, and the retained setting then improves monotonically with the thread count, gaining about a quarter of its final gap and reducing the seed dispersion by nearly half between 1 and 16 threads. At equal single-threaded budget the two encodings are close, and the small pooled edge of exact evaluation comes from that same hardest instance, so the practical advantage of the discretization is thread scaling rather than fidelity traded for speed. These descriptive results support multi-threading as a way to improve solution quality and stability when the model can exploit it, and they show that binding-level constraints on external evaluation must be measured, not assumed.
item.dc:creator: Florian Rascoussier

item.title: A note on the complexity of random subspace model-based methods for derivative-free optimization
item.description: arXiv:2608.17307v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate that, with a suitable rescaling, using Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms (JLTs) in the random subspace model-based derivative-free optimization (DFO) algorithm from [Cartis & Roberts, Math. Prog. 199 (2023)] achieves an improved first-order worst-case evaluation complexity bound compared to 'unscaled' JLTs. This improved bound does not require any modification to the original algorithm or complexity analysis, and matches the best-known bound in terms of dimension dependence for model-based DFO (e.g. achieved by [Scheinberg & Chaudhry, ICM 2026] using Haar matrices in a similar framework). A similarly refined analysis of the analogous second-order subspace method from [Cartis & Roberts, Opt. Meth. & Softw. (2026)] shows that using suitably scaled JLTs to generate the subspaces gives a better complexity bound, which improves over full-space methods only if the problem has low effective rank.
item.dc:creator: Coralia Cartis, Lindon Roberts

item.title: Optimal Loss Allocation and Reflected Free Boundaries in Systemic Risk
item.description: arXiv:2608.18113v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a singular mean-field control problem in which a central planner allocates losses generated by bank defaults to maximize terminal system health. Every generated loss must be borne by the surviving banks, without external capital. We prove that a cutoff, or "taxing-the-richest" rule is optimal for every non-decreasing concave terminal payoff, including the survival indicator. We construct the continuous-time optimizer by solving a time-discretized problem and passing to the limit, and establish its uniqueness in law for every non-constant payoff. The optimal flow is characterized by a novel reflected free-boundary problem. We establish well-posedness in a probabilistic solution class and prove positive-time smoothness of both the free boundary and the density of surviving banks. The main difficulty is the dependence of the limiting feedback on a moving support endpoint, which is unstable under Wasserstein convergence. We address this through stochastic-order comparisons, compactness estimates for the cutoff boundaries, and an augmented call-function formulation.
item.dc:creator: Yucheng Guo, Qinxin Yan

item.title: Anytime Solver Evaluation with a Normalized Signed Primal Integral and Explicit Reference Policies - Extended Version
item.description: arXiv:2608.18288v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Anytime solvers return usable solutions before they terminate and improve them while time remains. Their progress is commonly summarized by a primal integral, a final gap, or convergence curves. Each summary leaves consequential choices open: how to score a run before its first feasible solution, whether poor incumbents are truncated, and whether the reference value is updated after the experiment or version-frozen beforehand. These choices become visible when runs produce no valid incumbent or improve a published best-known value. We study a normalized signed primal integral built from a bounded relative gap. It assigns an intrinsic worst value to an empty run, requires no acceptance threshold, and assigns negative instantaneous gaps to incumbents that beat a frozen reference. We compare the smooth difference-over-sum kernel with a signed version of Berthold's max-normalized gap and use the former as a working default. We also distinguish analysis-time from version-frozen reference policies and recommend reading the score with the raw final gap, mean convergence curve, and target-attainment curve. We evaluate these choices on a five-arm routing campaign and two model-fidelity ladders. The two signed kernels preserve every panel ordering in this study, whereas a common acceptance threshold compresses the distances between arms and reverses one panel ordering. Updating 54 of the 212 reference values changes score levels and removes all negative scores, while leaving the observed panel orderings unchanged. An exploratory screen also identifies 12 panel comparisons in which similar integral scores conceal materially different endpoints or attainment rates. The implementation, frozen inputs, and generators are openly released.
item.dc:creator: Florian Rascoussier, Romain Billot, Lina Fahed, Christine Solnon

item.title: Sum-of-Squares Certificates for Copositive Matrices via Recursive Identities: The de Klerk-Pasechnik Conjecture and Hoffman-Pereira Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2609.01010v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the conjecture by de Klerk and Pasechnik (2002), claiming that the semidefinite bounds $\vartheta^{(r)}(G)(r\geq 0)$ for the stability number $\alpha(G)$ are exact at $r=\alpha(G)-1$, by exhibiting an explicit sum-of-squares certificate. This certificate allows us to recover a known characterization of the minimizers of the Motzkin-Straus formulation for $1/\alpha(G)$. Additionally, we give sum-of-squares copositivity certificates for the matrices satisfying the Hoffman-Pereira sign condition, a crucial condition for characterizing copositive matrices with $\{-1,0,1\}$ entries.
item.dc:creator: Jineon Baek, Luis Felipe Vargas

item.title: Strong Consistency, Optimal Tracking and Sharp Rates for the {\AA}str\"om-Wittenmark Self-Tuning Regulator with Unknown Input Gain
item.description: arXiv:2609.11831v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study strong consistency and optimal tracking of the Astrom-Wittenmark self-tuning regulator with unknown input gain. Existing results establish consistency of all parameter estimates for the unmodified recursion under additional growth conditions on reference information. Other approaches obtain stability and optimal tracking by adjusting the estimates used in feedback or adding decaying probing signals. For a class of minimum-phase linear systems with martingale difference noise, ordinary least squares (LS) with certainty-equivalent control achieves stability and optimal tracking almost surely for each bounded reference, provided the recursion is well defined. No reference excitation, adjustment of feedback estimates or added probing is required. When at least two parameters are estimated, all parameter estimates are strongly consistent, with squared norm of the estimation error $O(\log\log\log n/\log n)$ almost surely. A law of the iterated logarithm under zero reference shows that this rate cannot in general be improved. We also derive a logarithm law for cumulative squared tracking residuals, with an explicit dependence of the leading term on reference energy. A chi-square limit yields asymptotically exact parameter confidence ellipsoids for each bounded reference. The proof combines a logarithmic lower bound on the cumulative squared difference between an auxiliary LS prediction of the noise and the reference with estimates from the LS recursion. If the gain estimate were inconsistent, these bounds would yield incompatible estimates for the same weighted sum of squares, establishing gain consistency without assuming stability.
item.dc:creator: Zhaobo Liu

item.title: Sharp Linear Bounds and Exponential Separation for Single-Flip Methods in Absolute Value Equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.12763v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rohn's sign-accord algorithm is a classical single-coordinate sign-flip method for $Ax-|x|=b$, selecting the least-index mismatched coordinate at each step. We construct rational instances on which this rule requires exactly $2^{n-1}-1$ flips from natural initialization, even when both $\|A^{-1}\|_1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty$ are arbitrarily small. We propose two alternative selection rules, Gauss--Southwell and steepest single flipping, which require only one flip on the same instances. A discrete potential framework with positive polarity factors identifies solutions with global maximizers. Under positive polarity with ratio $\kappa$ and $r=\|A^{-1}\|_\infty<1$, both rules terminate from any initial signature after at most $\lfloor s\kappa(1+r)/(1-r)\rfloor$ flips, where $s$ is the number of nonzero solution coordinates. For fixed $\eta_1<1/2$ and $\eta_2<1$, both rules have worst-case flip complexity $O(n)$ on the class $\|A^{-1}\|_1\le\eta_1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty\le\eta_2$. An $n-1$ lower bound from natural initialization shows that this linear order is sharp. Under stronger, explicit sign-correction conditions, each rule makes exactly as many flips as there are initially incorrect signs among the nonzero solution components. Thus, each rule makes at most \(n\) flips, and this bound is optimal. A five-dimensional example requiring six greedy flips shows that the bound of $n$ does not extend to the entire common small-norm class. Building on Radons--Rump sign certificates, we further develop three classes of sign-flip algorithms using elimination guidance, cyclic scanning, and randomized $m$-flipping. Under $\rho(|A^{-1}|)<1/2$, we prove at most $n$ flips for elimination guidance, $n^2$ inspections for cyclic scanning, and $O(n^2/m)$ expected batch updates for randomized $m$-flipping. Exact computations and retained paired experiments distinguish flip counts from computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Cairong Chen, Yong Xia

item.title: Matching Higher-Order Oracle Complexity for Smooth Monotone Variational Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2609.13462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish near-optimal higher-order oracle bounds for smooth monotone variational inequalities. For fixed $p\ge2$, let $F$ be monotone on a known compact convex set $X$ of diameter at most $D$, with $\operatorname{Lip}(D^{p-1}F)\le L_p$. Each feasible query returns the complete jet $(F,DF,\ldots,D^{p-1}F)$, and the goal is to find $x$ with tangent residual $\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x)+N_X(x))\le\varepsilon$. Writing $Q=L_pD^p/\varepsilon$, we improve the $\widetilde O_p(Q^{1/p})$ upper bound of Chen et al. to $\widetilde O_p(Q^{2/(3p-1)})$ via a dimension-independent deterministic algorithm that returns an explicit tangent-residual certificate. We prove a matching $\Omega_p(Q^{2/(3p-1)})$ lower bound for arbitrary adaptive deterministic algorithms and randomized algorithms with per-instance success probability at least $2/3$, without span or tensor-update restrictions. Hence the high-dimensional worst-case oracle complexity is $\widetilde\Theta_p((L_pD^p/\varepsilon)^{2/(3p-1)})$. The same method applies to smooth convex--concave minimax problems, improving the fixed-geometry accuracy exponent from $4/(3p+1)$ to $2/(3p-1)$ and matching the known lower-bound exponent.
item.dc:creator: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: Near-Optimal Deterministic Exact-Value Complexity for Smooth Convex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.18230v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the deterministic oracle complexity of smooth convex optimization when the algorithm receives only exact function values. The objective is a globally $\beta$-smooth convex function, all queries and the final output are restricted to the Euclidean ball of radius $R$, and the unique minimizer lies in the ball of radius $R/2$. We establish an upper bound of $O(d\sqrt{\beta R^2/\epsilon})$ using coordinate finite differences together with an error-robust accelerated projected method. Our main contribution is a matching lower bound, up to the high-accuracy saturation of the construction: any deterministic adaptive value-oracle algorithm requires $\Omega\!\left(d\min\{\sqrt{\beta R^2/\epsilon},(d/\log(ed))^{1/3}\}\right)$ queries. Consequently, the minimax oracle complexity is $\Theta(d\sqrt{\beta R^2/\epsilon})$ throughout the moderate-accuracy regime $\beta R^2(\log(ed)/d)^{2/3}\leq\epsilon\leq c\beta R^2$ for a universal constant $c>0$. The lower bound must account for the fact that a single exact real value can encode arbitrarily much information. To overcome this difficulty, we construct a single fixed smooth convex hard instance using a Moreau-smoothed biased max chain, an exact prefix-shielding mechanism, and batched delayed rotations. These techniques preserve consistency with the full adaptive transcript and establish the optimality of the square-root complexity branch for deterministic bounded-query algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: Near-Optimal Exact-Value Zeroth-Order Complexity for Smooth Strongly Convex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.18728v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study deterministic adaptive optimization of globally $\beta$-smooth, $\mu$-strongly convex functions using exact scalar function values. Queries and outputs lie in $B_2^d(R)$, and the minimizer lies in $B_2^d(R/2)$. Set $\kappa=\beta/\mu$, $Q=\beta R^2/\epsilon$, and $D_d=(d/\log(ed))^{1/3}$. For sufficiently large $d$ and $0<\epsilon\le c_\epsilon\beta R^2$, the minimax value complexity $N_\epsilon$ satisfies \[ \begin{aligned} N_\epsilon &\ge c d\min\{\sqrt Q,\sqrt\kappa,D_d\},\\ N_\epsilon &\le C d\min\left\{ \sqrt Q,\sqrt\kappa[1+\log_+(Q/\kappa)] \right\}, \end{aligned} \] where $c,C,c_\epsilon>0$ are universal constants and $\log_+(t)=\max\{0,\log t\}$. The lower bound uses an exactly shielded smooth chain and batched delayed rotations; the upper bound combines finite differences, acceleration, and restart. When $\min\{Q,\kappa\}\le D_d^2$, these bounds match up to constants in the accuracy-dominated regime $Q\le\kappa$ and at constant relative accuracy $\epsilon=\Theta(\mu R^2)$. For arbitrarily higher accuracy in the range $\kappa\le D_d^2$, the bounds differ by at most $1+\log(\mu R^2/\epsilon)$; the optimal accuracy dependence remains unresolved in general.
item.dc:creator: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: Second-Order Stationarity with Common Random Losses: Matching Tolerance Bounds
item.description:
arXiv:2609.28238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish tight polynomial tolerance bounds for stochastic second-order stationarity when each fresh oracle response is a derivative of one common random scalar loss. For a population objective $F$ with Lipschitz gradient and Hessian, the target is $\|
abla F(x)\|\le \epsilon$ and $\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 F(x))\ge -\gamma$, with independent tolerances $\epsilon,\gamma>0$. Under bounded gradient variance and almost-surely bounded Hessian error, the minimax number of fresh gradient or Hessian-vector-product calls is $\widetilde{\Theta}\!\left(\epsilon^{-3}+\gamma^{-5}ight)$. The characterization fixes positive gap, smoothness, and noise parameters, suppresses logarithmic factors, and allows dimension to grow within an explicit polynomial envelope. The upper bound removes the mixed term $\epsilon^{-2}\gamma^{-2}$ from the earlier fresh-HVP guarantee. Direct random-line Hessian estimates and a dyadic gradient tracker separate gradient drift from randomly signed curvature motion. The lower bound realizes the endpoint costs through globally defined smooth random losses: a smooth partition localizes scalar noise without a chain-length penalty, while exact cancellation limits the information in the entire response. Consequently, the same tolerance exponents hold even for joint value, gradient, and full-Hessian responses with bounded value variance. For a population Hessian with H"older exponent $
u\in(0,1]$, fresh gradient/HVP complexity becomes $\widetilde{\Theta}\!\left(\epsilon^{-3}+\gamma^{-(3+2/
u)}ight)$ under the corresponding dimension envelope.
item.dc:creator: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: Near-Optimal Higher-Order Oracle Complexity for Convex--Concave Minimax Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.28246v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For smooth convex--concave minimax optimization, the higher-order lower bound of Chen et al. (2026) applies to a restricted tensor-algorithm class with prescribed regularized Taylor-model updates. We establish the same bound for arbitrary adaptive deterministic and randomized algorithms, matching, up to logarithmic factors, the upper bound of Zhang et al. (2026). Fix an integer $p\ge 2$ and let $L_p>0$ bound the Lipschitz constant of the objective's $p$-th derivative on a compact convex product domain of diameter at most $D_Z>0$. Each feasible query returns the objective value and all derivatives through order $p$. For accuracy $\epsilon>0$, set $Q_{\mathrm{tan}}=L_pD_Z^p/\epsilon$ for tangent residual and $Q_{\mathrm{gap}}=L_pD_Z^{p+1}/\epsilon$ for saddle gap. Let $T_E^{\mathrm{det}}(\epsilon)$ and $T_E^{\mathrm{rand}}(\epsilon)$ denote the high-dimensional minimax query complexities for criterion $E\in\{\mathrm{tan},\mathrm{gap}\}$, with randomized success probability at least $2/3$ on every instance. Our lower bounds and the existing upper bound give $c_pQ_E^{2/(3p-1)}\le T_E^{\mathrm{rand}}(\epsilon)\le T_E^{\mathrm{det}}(\epsilon)\le C_pQ_E^{2/(3p-1)}[1+\log(3+Q_E)]^{6(p-1)}$ for sufficiently large $Q_E$, where $c_p,C_p>0$ depend only on $p$. Thus the same accuracy exponent holds beyond tensor update rules, even for randomized queries and arbitrary feasible outputs. The proof constructs a scalar convex--concave chain with exactly flat gates that hide complete derivative information. Direct product-domain error witnesses and adaptive transcript arguments establish the lower bounds for both criteria.
item.dc:creator: Yanyi Li, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: DC decompositions and cutting-plane approximation: geometry and complexity
item.description: arXiv:2609.28319v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how Difference of Convex (DC) decomposition affects cutting-plane approximation in global optimization. For a smooth decomposition $f = g-h$, let $d$ be the dimension of the span of all Hessian ranges of $g$ over the convex hull of a compact feasible set. The smallest attainable dimension equals the minimum rank of a constant positive semidefinite matrix majorizing the Hessians of $f$ on that convex hull, and is attained by a quadratic first component. Retaining earlier gradient cuts and accepting new cuts only when the model error exceeds $\epsilon$ gives an $O(\epsilon^{-d/2})$ bound on accepted cuts.
